The preliminary case-control study suggests that "high-risk" human papillomaviruses (HPVs) cannot be detected in human breast milk. The study found that there were no mucosal 'high-risk' HPV types present in human breast milk. This indicates that exposure to high-risk HPVs may not lead to the development of breast cancer in infants or children, at least based on this limited study.

While further research is needed to fully understand the relationship between prenatal and perinatal exposures toHPV and breast cancer risk, this preliminary findings suggest caution when considering routine screening for HPV in human breast milk.
